portable_contracts.old_guidance: Nodes should expose text, type, source_position, and children before reaching merge orchestration.
portable_contracts.current_contract: Parser/provider output is projected into the normalized tree_haver node tree with progressive metadata and capabilities.

portable_contracts.old_guidance: Signature maps must preserve duplicate signatures and consume matches with a per-signature cursor.
portable_contracts.current_contract: Duplicate signatures are matched 1:1 in order unless a fixture-backed refiner or profile changes the match.

portable_contracts.old_guidance: Nested container merges recurse inside the matched container instead of flattening the whole file.
portable_contracts.current_contract: Recursive merge behavior is scoped by matched parent/container identity.

portable_contracts.old_guidance: Template-only nodes are inserted relative to surrounding matched nodes, not blindly prepended or appended.
portable_contracts.current_contract: Template-only insertion must be anchor-aware and fixture-backed for each family that claims it.

portable_contracts.old_guidance: Use shared comment, layout, trailing-group, partial-template, detector, and text fallback helpers before writing one-off code.
portable_contracts.current_contract: Reusable behavior belongs in tree_haver, ast-merge, ast-crispr, ast-template, or a family layer before a leaf provider grows private helpers.

ruby_only_or_adapter_conveniences.current_contract: Ruby adapters should preserve this where useful, but cross-language providers expose explicit structured request/profile fields.

ruby_only_or_adapter_conveniences.old_guidance: Choose inline SmartMerger or SmartMerger plus ConflictResolver.
ruby_only_or_adapter_conveniences.current_contract: This remains useful Ruby implementation advice but is not the portable implementation shape.

retired_requirements.old_guidance: A new gem implements SmartMerger, FileAnalysis, MergeResult, and often ConflictResolver/Emitter classes.
retired_requirements.current_contract: Portable conformance is expressed through fixtures, provider profiles, normalized trees, edit requests, and execution reports.

retired_requirements.old_guidance: Register each gem with Ast::Merge::RSpec::MergeGemRegistry for dependency tags.
retired_requirements.current_contract: Family/provider manifests and named-suite reports are the portable registry and conformance mechanism.

retired_requirements.old_guidance: Use old ast-merge RSpec shared examples as the primary new-gem test contract.
retired_requirements.current_contract: Fixture suites are the portable contract; Ruby-specific shared examples may still exist as local test helpers.

recommended_order: project parser output into the normalized tree
implement exact matching with duplicate cursor semantics
add recursive/container behavior when the format needs it
add template-only insertion and deletion policies
add comments, freeze directives, refiners, and partial-template behavior only after the basic contract is proven

verification.command: mise exec -C structuredmerge/ruby -- bundle exec rspec gems/ast-merge/spec/fixtures_integration_spec.rb
